topic: Roblox on-screen typography and text readability

claims.claim: Roblox's current API reference recommends that rendered text, and specifically UITextSizeConstraint.MinTextSize, not be lower than 9 because it may be unreadable or invisible to many users. The 9 value is an official Roblox readability recommendation in API-reference prose; it is not documented as a runtime/Studio warning, an enforced API minimum, or a universal platform rule.
claims.scope: TextLabel on-screen text and UITextSizeConstraint.MinTextSize when constraining TextScaled text. The recommendation is expressed in Roblox API-reference documentation, not in a platform policy or conformance standard.
limitations: UITextSizeConstraint.MinTextSize itself defaults to 1, so the API permits values below 9.
The TextLabel sample sets TextSize as low as 5, further showing that 9 is not an enforced lower bound.
No current official source found documents a warning, error, or rejection triggered solely by a value below 9. This documentation review cannot exclude an undocumented or future Studio diagnostic.

Roblox calls the value a size in pixels in UITextSizeConstraint, while TextLabel.TextSize is described as line height in offsets; neither statement establishes equivalence to CSS pixels or to the body-height measurement used by Xbox accessibility guidance.

sources.title: UITextSizeConstraint | Roblox Creator Hub
sources.supports: States that values lower than 9 are not recommended for MinTextSize because text may not be readable to most users; also documents a default MinTextSize of 1.

sources.title: TextLabel | Roblox Creator Hub
sources.supports: States that text size is recommended to be no lower than 9 because it may not be visible to many users, while its TextSize sample iterates from 5 to 100.

claims.claim: TextLabel.TextSize controls the height of one rendered line in offsets, not typographic points. Roblox does not document a separate enforced minimum on the TextSize property.
claims.scope: TextLabel.TextSize; corresponding text classes have analogous properties, but this source directly establishes TextLabel behavior.
limitations: The API text does not define how an offset maps to physical size, viewing distance, DPI, or measured glyph body height.
The absence of a documented property bound is not proof that every value renders usefully.
PreferredTextSize and other rendering/layout behavior can alter effective presentation.

sources.title: TextLabel | Roblox Creator Hub
sources.supports: Defines TextSize as the height of one rendered line, in offsets rather than points; its published sample uses values beginning at 5.

claims.claim: UITextSizeConstraint constrains TextLabel, TextButton, or TextBox text between MinTextSize and MaxTextSize when parented to the text object; it is intended for use with TextScaled. MinTextSize defaults to 1, MaxTextSize defaults to 1000, and the minimum must not exceed the maximum.
claims.scope: UITextSizeConstraint parented to supported Roblox text GuiObjects, especially with TextScaled enabled.
limitations: The defaults are API defaults, not readability recommendations.
A constraint caps scaling; it does not by itself establish a typographic hierarchy or guarantee readability against a particular background.

sources.title: UITextSizeConstraint | Roblox Creator Hub
sources.supports: Documents supported GuiObjects, intended TextScaled use, dynamic lower/upper bounds, defaults, and ordering requirements.

claims.claim: With TextScaled enabled, TextSize is ignored, TextWrapped is automatically enabled, and text scales to fill the label. For on-screen UI Roblox recommends constraining the possible range, but more generally recommends avoiding TextScaled in favor of AutomaticSize because unconstrained scaling can make text unreadably small; Roblox also recommends not combining AutomaticSize and TextScaled on the same TextLabel.
claims.scope: TextLabel.TextScaled, especially on-screen UI rather than BillboardGui text.
limitations: The recommendation to avoid TextScaled is not an API prohibition.
BillboardGui is identified as a useful TextScaled case, so the advice is contextual rather than universal.
AutomaticSize changes container bounds rather than guaranteeing that surrounding layout can accommodate them.

sources.title: TextLabel | Roblox Creator Hub
sources.supports: Documents TextScaled behavior, recommends UITextSizeConstraint for on-screen use, recommends AutomaticSize instead, and warns that careless scaling can become unreadable.

claims.claim: Roblox provides a player Preferred Text Size setting. TextScaled text is not scaled by PreferredTextSize; UITextSizeConstraint caps the setting's effect; AutomaticSize can grow or shrink element bounds with the resized text; and wrapped text can add lines within the element's absolute-size limits.
claims.scope: Roblox player text-size preference and UI elements participating in the engine font-rendering pipeline.
limitations: This is accommodation behavior, not a default readable-size threshold.
Using TextScaled can bypass the player's PreferredTextSize adjustment, so a UI can be technically valid yet fail to honor the preference for that element.
The accessibility design page was obtained through the official Creator Hub web fallback because the Context7 results covered the API properties but not this complete accessibility guidance.

sources.title: Accessibility guidelines | Roblox Creator Hub
sources.supports: Documents GuiService.PreferredTextSize and its interaction with UITextSizeConstraint, TextScaled, AutomaticSize, TextWrapped, and text measurement APIs.

claims.claim: FontFace accepts Roblox's Font datatype, whose Weight property uses Enum.FontWeight. Roblox exposes nine enum values from Thin (100) through Heavy (900), with Regular (400) as the default; Font constructors accept a requested weight.
claims.scope: TextLabel.FontFace and other UI properties that use the Font datatype.
limitations: Enum availability does not establish that every font family contains a face for every enum weight.
Enum names and numeric values describe thickness, not semantic UI roles.
The API documentation does not establish a universal fallback/rendering rule for a requested weight absent from a family.

sources.title: Font | Roblox Creator Hub
sources.supports: Defines Font as family, weight, and style; documents Font.Weight, the Regular default, and constructors accepting FontWeight.

sources.title: FontWeight | Roblox Creator Hub
sources.supports: Lists Thin 100, ExtraLight 200, Light 300, Regular 400, Medium 500, SemiBold 600, Bold 700, ExtraBold 800, and Heavy 900.

sources.title: TextLabel | Roblox Creator Hub
sources.supports: Documents TextLabel.FontFace as a Font datatype property.

claims.claim: Actual font-face availability should be established per family rather than inferred from Enum.FontWeight: TextService:GetFamilyInfoAsync returns a family's Faces, and Roblox's sample enumerates each face's Weight and Style.
claims.scope: Runtime inspection of Roblox font-family assets.
limitations: The API can fail due to network errors and Roblox instructs callers to handle failure.
The returned family data reports faces; it does not prescribe which weight should represent body, label, heading, emphasis, or action text.
No current official API text found defines how rendering behaves when the requested weight is absent.

sources.title: TextService | Roblox Creator Hub
sources.supports: Documents GetFamilyInfoAsync and demonstrates iterating info.Faces to print each face's Weight and Style.

sources.title: Font | Roblox Creator Hub
sources.supports: States that each family contains a number of faces and each face has a weight and style.

claims.claim: Roblox's published design guidance uses size and boldness for hierarchy: headers and titles should be larger and bolder than body text, and color or bolding can highlight important information. It also says to prioritize legibility when selecting a font.
claims.scope: General Roblox experience UI visual language and information hierarchy.
limitations: This is qualitative guidance; it gives no text-size scale, weight-number mapping, ratio, maximum number of hierarchy levels, or specific roles for Medium/SemiBold/Bold.
It does not justify inferring semantic meaning from the FontWeight enum.
The UI/UX design page was obtained through the official Creator Hub web fallback because the Context7 design query did not return the complete page.

sources.title: UI and UX design | Roblox Creator Hub
sources.supports: Defines hierarchy of information, recommends larger/bolder headers and titles, permits bolding for important information, and prioritizes font legibility.

claims.claim: Roblox publishes a specific semantic mapping such as Regular for body, Medium for labels, SemiBold for controls, and Bold for headings.
claims.scope: Current Roblox Creator Hub typography, UI/UX, accessibility, Font, and FontWeight materials reviewed for this assignment.
limitations: Roblox publishes qualitative larger/bolder hierarchy guidance, but not a role-by-weight token system.
A project may define its own semantic weight tokens, but that would be a project design recommendation, not a Roblox engine fact.
Absence from the reviewed current official sources does not prove that no Roblox staff presentation or unpublished internal design system has ever offered such a mapping.

sources.title: UI and UX design | Roblox Creator Hub
sources.supports: Provides only qualitative larger/bolder hierarchy and emphasis guidance.

sources.title: FontWeight | Roblox Creator Hub
sources.supports: Defines thickness choices and numeric values but assigns no UI semantics.

claims.claim: No current Roblox-specific rule for sentence case, title case, or all-caps usage was found in the reviewed official typography, accessibility, and UI/UX sources.
claims.scope: General on-screen Roblox UI copy and typography; this does not address language-specific localization rules.
limitations: The finding is limited to current official sources reviewed for this assignment.
It should not be converted into a claim that casing never affects readability.
High-authority external game guidance supplies a recommendation when Roblox is silent.

sources.title: UI and UX design | Roblox Creator Hub
sources.supports: Covers hierarchy, attention, visual language, text legibility, and consistency without prescribing casing.

sources.title: Accessibility guidelines | Roblox Creator Hub
sources.supports: Covers text size, contrast, and player preferences without prescribing casing.

claims.claim: When Roblox is silent on casing, Microsoft Xbox Accessibility Guidelines recommend proper sentence case instead of full caps or full lowercase for lines of text; one- or two-word labels are exempt. For subtitles/captions, Microsoft recommends mixed case because it is easier to read than uniform case.
claims.scope: Imported high-authority game-accessibility guidance, not a Roblox platform requirement.
limitations: The general rule explicitly exempts one- or two-word labels.
The subtitle rule applies to captions/subtitles, not necessarily every short HUD token.
This guidance cannot establish a universal Roblox MUST.

sources.title: Xbox Accessibility Guideline 101: Text display | Microsoft Learn
sources.supports: Recommends proper sentence case over full caps or full lowercase for text lines, with a one- or two-word-label exemption.

sources.title: Xbox Accessibility Guideline 104: Subtitles and captions | Microsoft Learn
sources.supports: Recommends mixed-case subtitle/caption text and states that it is easier to read than all one case.

claims.claim: Roblox TextLabel.LineHeight is an engine control expressed as a multiplier of the font em square. Its documented range is 1.0 to 3.0 and its default is 1.0. Roblox does not publish a separate readable line-height minimum in the reviewed design/accessibility guidance.
claims.scope: Multiline TextLabel rendering; the API fact does not itself prescribe an authored typographic leading scale.
limitations: The default 1.0 is an engine default, not evidence that 1.0 is optimal for reading.
LineHeight scales spacing using the em square, not the glyph body-height measurement used by Xbox text-size guidance.
Roblox does not expose letter-spacing or word-spacing properties alongside LineHeight in the cited TextLabel material.

sources.title: TextLabel | Roblox Creator Hub
sources.supports: Defines LineHeight as an em-square multiplier with range 1.0–3.0 and default 1.0.

sources.title: Accessibility guidelines | Roblox Creator Hub
sources.supports: Provides general text readability and scaling guidance but no numeric authored line-height recommendation.

claims.claim: For blocks longer than two lines, Xbox Accessibility Guideline 101 recommends configurability for line width and spacing; if configurability is absent, it suggests line spacing of at least 1.5, alongside limits/values for line width, paragraph spacing, letter spacing, and word spacing. WCAG 2.2's 1.5 line-height figure has a different scope: web content must survive a user override to that value without losing content or functionality; WCAG explicitly says authors are not required to use 1.5 as their default.
claims.scope: Xbox guidance is imported game-accessibility guidance; WCAG is imported web-accessibility guidance and is not directly a Roblox engine conformance requirement.
limitations: Xbox's 1.5 recommendation is for blocks over two lines at standard size when players cannot configure spacing.
WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.12 applies to markup technologies supporting user style overrides; it should not be misquoted as a mandatory authored line-height.
Language and writing-system differences can make some spacing metrics inapplicable.
Neither source creates a universal Roblox LineHeight rule.

sources.title: Xbox Accessibility Guideline 101: Text display | Microsoft Learn
sources.supports: Suggests configurable spacing or, when unavailable, 1.5 line spacing for blocks longer than two lines plus other spacing metrics.

sources.title: Understanding WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 1.4.12: Text Spacing | W3C
sources.supports: Requires no loss under specified user spacing overrides and explicitly states that content is not required to use those values by default.

claims.claim: Roblox exposes TextStrokeColor3 and TextStrokeTransparency for text outlines. The API recommends TextStrokeTransparency in the 0.75–1 range for a subtle effect and identifies UIStroke as a more powerful gradient-capable alternative; it does not claim that every text element should have an outline or that this range guarantees readability.
claims.scope: TextLabel text-stroke appearance; analogous properties exist on other Roblox text GuiObjects but this source directly establishes TextLabel.
limitations: The 0.75–1 range is an aesthetic recommendation for subtlety, not an accessibility contrast target.
Transparency compounds because the stroke is multiple renderings; effective contrast depends on stroke color and every background behind the text.
The API page does not provide a stroke-width readability minimum.

sources.title: TextLabel | Roblox Creator Hub
sources.supports: Documents stroke color/transparency, multiplicative rendering, the 0.75–1 subtle-effect recommendation, and UIStroke as an alternative.

claims.claim: For text over variable gameplay backgrounds, Xbox guidance treats borders/outlines and solid or opacity-adjustable text backgrounds as valid ways to improve contrast. It recommends measuring text against the lowest-contrast area of a non-solid background; subtitle guidance specifically recommends a configurable solid background and opacity.
claims.scope: Imported game-accessibility guidance for dynamic game scenes, HUD text, and captions; not a mandate to outline all Roblox text.
limitations: An outline is a contrast technique, not a substitute for measuring the resulting presentation.
Microsoft presents multiple approaches—background, color options, high-contrast mode, and borders—rather than making outline universal.
Caption-background configurability is specifically scoped to captions/subtitles.
The guidance does not prescribe Roblox TextStrokeTransparency or UIStroke values.

sources.title: Xbox Accessibility Guideline 102: Contrast | Microsoft Learn
sources.supports: Recommends solid/adjustable-opacity backgrounds, color options, high-contrast modes, and borders; requires measurement against the lowest-contrast background area.

sources.title: Xbox Accessibility Guideline 104: Subtitles and captions | Microsoft Learn
sources.supports: Recommends configurable solid subtitle backgrounds and 0–100% background opacity for readability across gameplay backgrounds.

claims.claim: Roblox's general accessibility guidance says small text can be difficult to read, increasing smaller labels makes them clearer to most players, and text/background colors should have sufficient contrast. That design page does not publish a numeric default text-size minimum or numeric contrast ratio.
claims.scope: General Roblox experience accessibility design, distinct from the API-reference recommendation of 9.
limitations: The examples are qualitative and do not define a measurement method.
The absence of a numeric threshold on this page does not erase the separate API-reference recommendation of 9.
'Sufficient contrast' is not quantified by Roblox in the cited page; numeric ratios below are imported external guidance.
The page was obtained via official Creator Hub web fallback after Context7 did not return the full accessibility material.

sources.title: Accessibility guidelines | Roblox Creator Hub
sources.supports: Uses low-vision examples to recommend larger small labels and sufficient foreground/background contrast, without numeric minima.

claims.claim: Microsoft Xbox Accessibility Guideline 101 supplies external game-specific numeric defaults when Roblox guidance is insufficient: at 1080p it recommends at least 26 measured body-height pixels on console and 18 on PC/VR; for mobile/game streaming it recommends 18 pixels at 100 DPI, scaling linearly with DPI. It also recommends allowing scaling to 200% of those default minima without loss of content, functionality, or meaning.
claims.scope: Imported Xbox game-accessibility guidance, measured from rendered ascender-to-descender body height under the stated resolution/DPI contexts; not Roblox TextSize values.
limitations: These numbers are not Roblox requirements and must not be relabeled as Roblox minimum TextSize values.
The measurement method differs from Roblox's documented TextSize/MinTextSize terminology, so direct numeric substitution is unsupported.
Viewing distance, resolution, and DPI are part of the Xbox scope; 18 or 26 is not universal across all displays.
Xbox permits players to scale smaller at their discretion after providing an accessible default.

sources.title: Xbox Accessibility Guideline 101: Text display | Microsoft Learn
sources.supports: Defines the measurement method, platform/resolution/DPI minimum default sizes, and 200% scaling guidance.

claims.claim: High-authority external contrast guidance is numeric but not Roblox-specific: Xbox XAG 102 recommends 4.5:1 for standard important text and 3:1 for its defined large text; WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 likewise requires 4.5:1 for ordinary web text and 3:1 for large-scale web text. WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.4 requires web text to resize to 200% without loss of content or functionality.
claims.scope: Xbox values are imported game-accessibility guidance; WCAG values are imported web-accessibility conformance criteria. Neither is an official Roblox numeric rule.
limitations: Xbox and WCAG define 'large text' differently and use context-specific measurements; their thresholds must not be mixed without preserving those definitions.
WCAG applies to web content, not automatically to Roblox-rendered game UI.
Roblox's official accessibility page says 'sufficient contrast' but does not adopt these ratios explicitly.
Contrast compliance does not alone establish readable text size, font choice, spacing, or viewing-distance suitability.

sources.title: Xbox Accessibility Guideline 102: Contrast | Microsoft Learn
sources.supports: Provides game-specific 4.5:1 and 3:1 contrast recommendations and contextual large-text definitions.

sources.title: Understanding WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 1.4.3: Contrast (Minimum) | W3C
sources.supports: States WCAG Level AA text contrast thresholds and web large-scale-text exceptions.

sources.title: Understanding WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 1.4.4: Resize Text | W3C
sources.supports: Requires web text to resize up to 200% without loss of content or functionality.

conflicts: The apparent numeric conflict between Roblox's 9 recommendation and Xbox's 18/26-pixel defaults is a scope and measurement conflict, not evidence that one source supersedes the other: Roblox discusses TextSize/MinTextSize readability in engine terms, while Xbox measures rendered body height under specified resolution/DPI and viewing contexts.

Roblox documents TextScaled as useful, especially for BillboardGui, while also recommending that on-screen UI avoid it in favor of AutomaticSize. This is contextual guidance, not a factual contradiction.

Roblox's TextStrokeTransparency 0.75–1 recommendation targets a subtle visual effect; Xbox's border/background guidance targets reliable contrast. A subtle stroke may be insufficient for accessibility, but the sources address different goals.

Xbox suggests authored 1.5 line spacing for longer blocks when configurability is absent; WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.12 does not require authors to use 1.5 by default and instead requires web layouts to survive a user's spacing override. These statements are compatible once scope is preserved.
unresolved: No current official Roblox numeric type scale, line-length target, authored body-text line-height recommendation, or weight-by-semantic-role mapping was found.
No current official Roblox casing rule for general on-screen UI was found.

No current official documentation of a Studio/runtime warning triggered solely by TextSize or MinTextSize below 9 was found; the API documentation instead presents 9 as a recommendation and permits lower values.
Official documentation establishes that family faces can be queried, but does not establish a universal fallback behavior when a requested FontWeight face is absent.
A direct equivalence between Roblox TextSize/MinTextSize numbers and Xbox's screenshot-measured ascender-to-descender pixel body height is not established and should not be inferred.
